title: Spring transactions
context: How do Spring transactions work, and what are the common pitfalls?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `@Transactional` makes Spring open a transaction around a public method through a proxy. Propagation says how it joins an existing transaction: REQUIRED, the default, joins it or starts one, while REQUIRES_NEW always starts a new one. By default, rollback happens for unchecked exceptions and errors, not for checked exceptions, unless `rollbackFor` says otherwise. Pitfalls: calling a @Transactional method from the same class skips the proxy, private methods are not proxied, and catching the exception inside the method hides the rollback.

points.title: Proxy and self-calls
points.why: A transactional method called from inside its own class runs with no transaction.

points.title: Rollback rules
points.why: Only RuntimeException and Error roll back by default. Checked exceptions commit unless rollbackFor is set.

points.title: Swallowed exceptions
points.why: If the exception is caught and not rethrown, Spring sees no failure and commits.
